title: Things to Do in Pokhara: Sights, Prices and Timings
meta_description: Things to do in Pokhara with prices: Phewa boating, Sarangkot sunrise, paragliding, zipline, caves, Peace Pagoda, Begnas Lake, short hikes and a 3-day plan.
summary: The essential things to do in Pokhara are a dawn row on Phewa Lake to Tal Barahi, sunrise at Sarangkot, a tandem paragliding flight (about ₹6,500–8,500), the World Peace Pagoda at sunset, Davis Falls and Gupteshwor Cave, and the Mountain Museum. Three days covers them; add a fourth for Begnas Lake or Australian Camp.

sections.heading: On the water: Phewa Lake and Tal Barahi
paras: Phewa is the reason Pokhara grew into a holiday town, and an hour on it is the first thing to do. Painted wooden boats called doongas wait at the Barahi ghat in central Lakeside, with hourly rates fixed by the boat cooperative at roughly NPR 1,000–1,500 per boat with an oarsman. A boat seats four to six, so families share one. Go before 8 am, when the water is still and Machhapuchhre is reflected in it; by late morning the breeze breaks the surface.

Five minutes out is Tal Barahi, a two-roofed pagoda temple to the goddess Barahi on a small island. Hindu visitors bring flowers and red powder, and on Saturdays there is a queue. For a longer outing, ask to be dropped at the south shore landing, 20–30 minutes away, and climb the forest trail to the World Peace Pagoda. Kayaks and paddle boards can also be hired at Lakeside for about NPR 500–1,000 an hour.

sections.heading: Sunrise and viewpoints
paras: Sarangkot at dawn is the classic Pokhara morning. Your car leaves Lakeside about 75 minutes before sunrise, climbs for 30–45 minutes to a car park below the ridge at about 1,600 m, and you walk 10–15 minutes up steps to the viewing terraces. As the light comes, Dhaulagiri, Annapurna South, Machhapuchhre and Annapurna II catch the sun in turn while mist still lies on the lake. A private car costs about NPR 1,500–2,500 return, plus a small entry fee.

The World Peace Pagoda, a white Buddhist stupa built by Japanese monks on the ridge south of the lake at about 1,100 m, is the best sunset spot. It is free to enter; shoes come off on the upper terrace and silence is expected. For a bigger panorama with fewer people, Australian Camp at about 2,060 m is a 45-minute drive to Kande and a 1–1.5 hour climb, best as an overnight stay so that you see both sunset and sunrise.

sections.heading: Adventure: paragliding, zipline and more
paras: Pokhara is Nepal's adventure sports base, and most activities are bookable a day ahead at Lakeside offices. Tandem paragliding from Sarangkot is the most popular: a licensed pilot flies you for 20–30 minutes over the valley, landing beside the lake. No experience is needed. The ZipFlyer drops about 600 m from the Sarangkot ridge towards Hemja along a 1.8 km cable at speeds of up to 140 km/h. Ultralight aircraft climb higher towards the Annapurna foothills, and the bungee tower at Hemja gives a few seconds of freefall over the Hemja valley.

All of these depend on weather. Paragliding and ultralights fly mostly from September or October to May and are largely paused in the monsoon; every activity has weight and health limits. People with heart conditions, recent back injuries or pregnancy should not take part. Prices below are typical 2026 rates per person; Indian visitors are often quoted lower rupee rates, and every figure changes by season, so check current status before you travel.

sections.heading: Caves, waterfalls and museums
paras: A cluster of sights near the airport and the Siddhartha Highway fills a morning. Davis Falls, or Patale Chhango, is where Phewa's outflow drops into a deep slot and vanishes underground; it is fullest from late August to October. Across the road, a spiral staircase leads down into Gupteshwor Mahadev Cave, a Shiva shrine with a passage that ends behind the same waterfall. Entry to each is roughly NPR 100–200, with lower rates for SAARC nationals.

North of the city, Mahendra Cave and the Bat Cave (Chamero Gufa) sit a few minutes apart near Batulechaur. Mahendra Cave is lit and has a Shiva shrine; the Bat Cave is unlit, home to thousands of bats, and its narrow exit requires a short squeeze, so bring a torch. The International Mountain Museum at Ratopahiro covers the 8,000 m peaks, climbing history and mountain peoples, and needs about two hours. Entry is about NPR 250 for SAARC visitors and NPR 500 for others.

sections.heading: Old Pokhara, temples and Tibetan settlements
paras: Most visitors never leave Lakeside, but the older city has more character. Bindhyabasini temple, on a small rise above the Old Bazaar, is Pokhara's main Durga shrine and is busiest on Saturdays, when families bring animals for sacrifice. The streets below keep tiled Newar shophouses from the town's trading days. Near Mahendrapul, the Seti Gandaki has cut a gorge so narrow and deep that the river is barely visible from the bridge.

Pokhara also has Tibetan refugee settlements dating from the 1960s. Tashiling, near Davis Falls, and the larger settlement at Hemja on the road north both have monasteries, carpet workshops and handicraft stalls. A morning visit, when monks are at prayer, is the most rewarding. Bargain politely; prices for singing bowls and carpets vary widely with quality.

sections.heading: Day trips beyond the city
paras: Within an hour of Lakeside are several quieter outings that suit a fourth or fifth day. Each can be done as a half day or full day by private car, which costs roughly NPR 4,000–7,000 for the day depending on distance. The hill options are best between October and April, when trails are dry and the peaks are clear.
list: Begnas Lake, 15 km east: calm rowing at NPR 700–1,200 per boat per hour, fish lunches on the shore and a ridge walk to Rupa Lake
Dhampus, about 1 hour by jeep: Gurung village homestays at about 1,650 m with sunrise over Annapurna South
Australian Camp, 45 minutes to Kande then 1–1.5 hours on foot: forest trail and one of the closest views of Machhapuchhre
Panchase, 2–3 hours by jeep: the highest viewpoint near Pokhara at 2,517 m, with sacred ponds and orchid forest
Sirubari, 3–4 hours by road: a Gurung homestay village with cultural evenings, best as an overnight

sections.heading: A 3-day Pokhara plan
paras: This is the order we use in our 3-night Pokhara package, which keeps each day to one early start and leaves room for weather. If the first morning is cloudy, swap days one and two so that Sarangkot gets the clearer dawn.
list: Day 1: arrive, check in at Lakeside, late-afternoon boat to Tal Barahi, dinner by the lake
Day 2: Sarangkot sunrise, breakfast, Davis Falls, Gupteshwor Cave, Mountain Museum, Bindhyabasini, Peace Pagoda at sunset
Day 3: paragliding or zipline in the morning, Begnas Lake or the Tibetan settlement in the afternoon
Day 4: early boat on Phewa if time allows, departure flight or drive

faqs.q: What are the top things to do in Pokhara?
faqs.a: The essentials are a morning boat to Tal Barahi on Phewa Lake, sunrise at Sarangkot, a tandem paragliding flight, the World Peace Pagoda at sunset, Davis Falls and Gupteshwor Cave, and the International Mountain Museum. Add Begnas Lake, the ZipFlyer or a short hike to Australian Camp if you have a fourth day.

faqs.q: How many days are enough to see Pokhara?
faqs.a: Three nights covers the main sights at a comfortable pace, with one early sunrise and one day for paragliding or a lake trip. Four nights lets you add Begnas Lake or an overnight at Australian Camp. Families arriving by road from Kathmandu should allow at least three nights, because the drive takes most of a day.

The World Peace Pagoda, Bindhyabasini temple, the Seti gorge viewpoints, the Lakeside promenade and the walk around the Old Bazaar are free. Tal Barahi temple is free to enter, though you pay for the boat to reach it. Sarangkot has a small entry fee at the viewing area, and Davis Falls, the caves and the museum charge tickets.

faqs.q: What can I do in Pokhara with kids?
faqs.a: Children enjoy the boat to Tal Barahi, the climbing wall and exhibits at the Mountain Museum, Davis Falls, Mahendra Cave and the Sarangkot sunrise. Older children who meet the weight limits can paraglide, often from about six years, or ride the ZipFlyer from about 35 kg. Hotels with pools help on hot afternoons in April and May.

faqs.q: What is there to do in Pokhara in the evening?
faqs.a: Watch sunset from the World Peace Pagoda or the lakeshore near Basundhara Park, then walk the Lakeside strip, where restaurants serve Nepali, Thakali, Indian and continental food and several have live music. Dinner for two costs about ₹1,200–2,500. Most places close by 11 pm, except during the Street Festival at New Year.

faqs.q: Is paragliding the best activity in Pokhara?
faqs.a: For most first-time visitors it is the highlight. A 20–30 minute tandem flight over Phewa Lake with the Annapurnas behind costs about ₹6,500–8,500 and needs no experience. If you prefer an engine and a higher route towards the mountains, choose an ultralight flight; if you want a quick thrill, the ZipFlyer takes about two minutes.

faqs.q: What to do in Pokhara on a rainy day?
faqs.a: Visit the International Mountain Museum, which needs about two hours, then Gupteshwor Cave and Davis Falls, which are at their fullest in the rain. Mahendra Cave, the Tibetan settlements and their workshops, and Bindhyabasini temple also work in wet weather. Lakeside cafes, yoga classes and spa treatments fill the gaps.

faqs.q: Can I see Pokhara in one day?
faqs.a: You can see the highlights in a long day: Sarangkot sunrise, a boat to Tal Barahi, Davis Falls, Gupteshwor Cave and the World Peace Pagoda at sunset. You will not have time for paragliding or the museum. With a 6–8 hour drive from Kathmandu each way, a single night is the minimum we suggest.

faqs.q: Are there hiking options near Pokhara?
faqs.a: Yes. The forest trail to the World Peace Pagoda takes 45 minutes from the south shore. Australian Camp is a 1–1.5 hour climb from Kande, and Dhampus links to it on a gentle path. Panchase, at 2,517 m, makes a good overnight. Australian Camp and Dhampus need an ACAP permit; check current status before you travel.
